correctness.rationale: Exact differentiation yields the density \(1-\lambda D_m(x,y)B_\theta(z)\). The factor \(B_\theta\) ranges over \([-r_\theta,1]\); the factor \(D_m\) ranges over \([-(m+1),m+1]\) for odd \(m\), and \([-M_m,m+1]\) for even \(m\). Fixing \(|x-y|\) reduces the even minimum to a quadratic critical-point equation. Independence of the two factors yields the necessary-and-sufficient density intervals, including both endpoints. A logarithmic inequality proves \(M_m/(m+1)>e^{-2}\), and strict monotonicity of \(r_\theta\) gives a unique transition. For \(m=2,\theta=1\), the exact range is \([-1/2,1/3]\). The companion program passed 118 supporting assertions; numerical diagnostics do not replace the proof for all parameters.
